tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which Imagelato projects they have, or a project's id is needed. Returns each project's id and name, 25 per page by default. Not for a project's processed images.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Use this when someone asks about one Imagelato project by name or id. Returns its id, name, logo URL and created and edited times, or not-found. Not for a quick look at its latest processed images.

tools.name: add_project
tools.description: Use this when someone wants a new Imagelato project to organize images and resize presets. Returns the new project's id, name and creation time and fires the project.created webhook. Each call creates another project. Not for adding a resize preset.

tools.name: list_batches
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which images a project has processed, or which resized and converted batches exist. Returns each batch's id, slug, output format and template id, 25 per page by default. Not for one batch's variant files and links.

tools.name: get_batch
tools.description: Use this when someone asks for the resized or converted versions of one processed image, or their links. Returns the batch's project, template, main URL, formats and sizes plus up to 20 variants with format, size and first-party URL. Not for resizing or converting a new image.

tools.name: delete_batch
tools.description: Use this when someone wants one processed image batch deleted for good. Returns the deleted batch's id, slug and project. Its original, main output and every resized or converted file are erased and the batch.deleted webhook fires, with no undo. Not for removing a resize preset.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which resize and format presets (templates) they have, optionally in one project. Returns each template's id, name, project, output formats and pixel widths, 25 per page by default. Not for the images processed with them.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: Use this when someone asks about one resize and format preset by name or id. Returns its project, output formats, pixel widths and created and edited times, or not-found. Not for changing it.

tools.name: add_template
tools.description: Use this when someone wants a new preset that resizes and converts images to set widths and formats in a project. Returns the new template; formats default to jpg and webp and widths to 512, 256, 128 and 64 pixels. Each call creates another preset. Not for editing a preset.

tools.name: update_template
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to rename a resize preset or change its output formats or widths. Returns the updated template after replacing only the fields given, and fires the template.updated webhook; it cannot move the preset to another project. Not for creating a preset.

tools.name: list_webhook_subscriptions
tools.description: Use this when someone asks whether their Imagelato webhooks are working, failing or disabled. Returns each endpoint's origin, subscribed events, active flag and consecutive failures, 25 per page by default; an endpoint is disabled after 20 failures in a row. Not for adding or editing a webhook.

tools.name: list_team_members
tools.description: Use this when someone asks who is on their Imagelato team and what role each person has. Returns each member's display name and roles, 25 per page by default (no emails, phone numbers or user ids). Not for inviting or removing members.

tools.name: show_project_overview
tools.description: Use this when someone wants a quick visual overview of one Imagelato project and its latest processed images. Returns a card with the project's name, logo and dates plus its 8 most recently processed batches with format, size and first-party links. Not for every batch in the project.

tools.name: open_imagelato
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to open Imagelato and browse their image projects, recent processed batches, image variants and resize presets in an interactive sidebar. Returns up to 100 projects to start from (no ownership data or credentials). Not for uploading, processing or generating images.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "open_imagelato" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_project, get_batch, list_team_members · Private data: list_batches, delete_batch, open_imagelato · Public sink: add_project, delete_batch, update_template, list_webhook_subscriptions · Destructive: list_batches, get_batch, delete_batch, list_templates, get_template, show_project_overview.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_project, get_batch, list_team_members · Private data: list_batches, delete_batch, open_imagelato · Public sink: add_project, delete_batch, update_template, list_webhook_subscriptions · Destructive: list_batches, get_batch, delete_batch, list_templates, get_template, show_project_overview

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
